To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the replacement of BF in bread formulations by CO and OO, in combination with the addition of flaxseed, soybean and wheat bran flour, improved the fatty acids profile of breads and their sensory characteristics.
the replacement of BF by CO and OO in bread formulations made with flaxseed flour, soybean flour and wheat bran, improved the fatty acid profile and sensory characteristics of the bread.

the use of flaxseed flour in breads with vegetable oil as fat replacer improved the FA profile of breads, and that the combination of flaxseed and soybean flours with olive oil was effective to improve sensory characteristics and overall acceptance of breads.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a healthy and nutritious bread with a better FA profile and with a high acceptance by consumers.
the development of breads with improved FA profile and good sensory acceptance.
the development of bread formulations, which allow the replacement of bovine fat with vegetable oils, maintaining the technological and sensory characteristics of the products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CO and OO can replace BF in bread formulations and improve its nutritional quality, with no significant changes in the technological and sensory characteristics of breads.
the breads made with CO and OO, in particular the bread with WF +FF + SB + CO, presented a better profile of fatty acids than the bread made with BF, and also had a good acceptance by consumers.

breads made from the mix of WF + SF and WF + Soybean oil (SO) + FF, and breads made from WF + WB and WF + OO + FF are good options for improving the FA profile and the sensory characteristics of breads.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of vegetable oil in bread formulations can be an interesting strategy for improving the nutritional quality of the product, without compromising the sensory acceptance.
bread made from the mixtures of flour with vegetable oils can improve the nutritional quality of breads.

the replacement of animal fat by vegetable oils in the formulation of breads made with flaxseed and wheat bran is a promising alternative for the improvement of fatty acids profile of breads, with good technological and sensory quality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to replace BF with CO or OO, in the formulation of breads with WF, FF and SF, without affecting their quality.
it is possible to obtain a bread with high nutritional quality and a good sensory acceptance using vegetable oils to substitute animal fat.
breads with WF, FF and SF fortified with CO and OO have a better FA profile and are acceptable from the sensory standpoint.
